text:
Karim: thinking out loud — ran into a weird race when preemptive fallback kicks in during oversubscribe. apps saw two different fallback models for the same request within 200ms.
Maya: ouch. is this the old stale route compat cache + concurrent policy-eval case?
Karim: yeah, looks like policy engine returned variant A, runtime started a short-lived lease, then fallback re-eval returned variant B and runtime applied a fallback swap mid-flight.
Sam: can you paste the minimal repro logs?
Karim: pasted below — note timestamps and the lease ids: 
```
2026-02-04T10:21:01.123Z policy-eval request=rt-42 eval_id=ee7 got=variant-A
2026-02-04T10:21:01.210Z runtime lease=start lease_id=L-100 tenant=T-22 model=variant-A
2026-02-04T10:21:01.300Z policy-eval request=rt-42 eval_id=ee8 got=variant-B (fallback)
2026-02-04T10:21:01.340Z runtime lease=swap lease_id=L-101 replace=L-100 model=variant-B
```
Karim: result is partial responses then model-change errors on client side.
Lena: we need an atomic handoff semantics for preemptive fallback. either the runtime must finish/abort existing lease before applying new model, or we need in-flight model pinning.
Maya: agree. tradeoffs: pinning increases tail latency (can't preempt), aborting increases error surface. Also need to consider cost: oversubscribe wants to move to cheaper variant quickly.
Sam: proposal: add a two-phase commit for a lease swap with a CAS on route generation. Pseudocode: 
```
// policy decides fallback
old = runtime.get_active_lease(req_id)
if CAS(lease_table[req_id], old, new_lease) {
  runtime.prepare(new_lease)
  runtime.commit(new_lease)
} else {
  // another actor raced; re-evaluate or attach to current lease
}
```
Sam: that keeps swap atomic at the route-table level. runtime.prepare could prefetch weights/kv cache for variant-B.
Lena: but CAS on every request might be hot. need batching or per-tenant gate.
ops-oncall: from ops POV prefer bounded retries and observability: metric for aborted-swaps, histogram of swap-latency, and an SLO for "model-stability per request". also add a feature-flag to toggle strict-atomic-swap.
Karim: what about eventual consistency approach: allow dual-writing kernel to serve both variants for 50ms window, then drain older variant? avoids errors while migrating.
Maya: dual-serving is neat but doubles GPU cost for the window. maybe only for low-traffic tenants or when difference in cost is small.
DevBot: perf-estimate: pre-warm + 50ms dual-serving adds ~0.7x VRAM pressure for ephemeral allocations on p100/80.
Lena: another angle: change policy engine to return compatibility hints, not direct assignments. runtime then chooses safe fallback if incompatible. i.e., policy -> {preferred: B, compatibleWith: [A,B]}
Karim: compatibility hints are attractive — pushes complexity to policy, but keeps runtime safe. downside: policy must know runtime compat matrix.
Sam: could centralize compat matrix in a service (read-only cache) so both policy and runtime consult same source. updates via config push.
Maya: action items: 1) prototype CAS-based atomic swap in runtime (Sam), 2) add metrics for swaps and aborted-swaps (ops-oncall), 3) evaluate dual-serving cost for sample tenants (DevBot), 4) spike compatibility-hint API and matrix (Lena).
Karim: I'll also add a short RFC describing invariants (atomic swap vs pin vs dual serve) and recommended default: CAS-swap + 100ms drain window for safer corner cases.
ops-oncall: please include rollback plan for toggling back to old behavior if we see client-side errors. @oncall — FYI. :eyes:
Maya: cool. if anyone wants to pair on the prototype ping me.
Sam: starting PR draft for CAS-swaps this afternoon. will link rough bench numbers.
Lena: adding compat-matrix spike to my calendar for next week.
Karim: thanks all — will follow up with RFC link once drafted. :thumbsup:
